title: Inquest reveals details surrounding death of former rugby player Michael Martindale
excerpt: An inquest has revealed significant details surrounding the death of Michael Martindale, a former rugby league player, who was found dead in Oldham with multiple injuries.
body:
An inquest into the death of Michael Martindale, a former professional rugby league player, has revealed significant details about his injuries and the circumstances surrounding his death.

Martindale, 50, was discovered dead on 28 May 2025, in his flat on Eldon Street, Oldham, after relatives expressed concern for his welfare when he failed to respond to calls and messages.

The inquest, held at Rochdale Coroners' Court on 10 November 2026, heard that Martindale had a history of battling alcoholism and had experienced relapses in the weeks leading up to his death.

He was found on a sofa in his flat, with his front door unlocked and his phone and bank cards at the scene. Four individuals were arrested in connection with his death but were later released without charge after a thorough police investigation.

Detective Inspector Andy Barrett, who led the investigation, noted that while Martindale had sustained multiple bruises and a serious neck injury, there was no evidence linking the arrested individuals to the scene.

Pathologist Dr Jamie Robinson stated that the injuries could have resulted from a heavy fall or blunt force trauma, but he could not determine the exact cause of death.

Toxicology tests indicated that Martindale had consumed alcohol prior to his death but was only slightly over the drink-drive limit.

Tributes to Martindale, known affectionately as 'Tricky', poured in from the local rugby community following his death. His son, Finbarr Martindale, described him as a much-loved father known for his 'witty one-liners' and 'infectious laugh'.

Coroner Michael Salt acknowledged the impact of Martindale's struggles with alcohol and remarked on the affection held for him by family and friends.
